glosses: The act of speaking in a quiet voice, especially without vibration of the vocal cords.

examples.text: I spoke in a near whisper.

glosses: A rumor.

examples.text: There are whispers of rebellion all around.

glosses: A faint trace or hint (of something).

examples.text: The soup had just a whisper of basil.

glosses: A low rustling sound, like that of the wind in leaves.
A private message to an individual in a chat room.

examples.text: The invisibility of private interactions in the form of whispers resolved an ethical concern in the research but reduced our ability to gauge the volume of interaction […]

glosses: To speak softly or under one's breath, so as to be heard only by one near at hand; to utter words without sonant breath; to talk without that vibration of the vocal cords which gives sonorous, or vocal, sound.

examples.text:
I can hear them whisper as we pass by
It's a bad sign, bad sign

glosses: To say (something) softly or under one's breath, so as to be heard only by one near at hand; to utter (something) without sonant breath, without that vibration of the vocal cords which gives sonorous, or vocal, sound.

examples.text: Whether he whispered sweet nothings to her in Stengelese is not known, but he did call her "the best catch I ever made in my career."

glosses: To mention privately and confidentially, or in a whisper.

examples.text: They might buzz and whisper it one to another.

glosses: To make a low, sibilant sound.

examples.text: the hollow, whispering breeze

[…] hear thy laurel whisper sweet
About the ledges of the hill.

glosses: To speak with suspicion or timorous caution; to converse in whispers, as in secret plotting.

examples.text: All that hate me whisper together against me.

glosses: To address in a whisper, or low voice.

examples.text: and whisper one another in the ear
where gentlest breezes whisper souls distressed

glosses: To prompt secretly or cautiously; to inform privately.

examples.text: He came to whisper Wolsey.
[A] simple youth whispered me that he was an Illuminé, and carried on an intercourse with the invisible world.

glosses: To send a private message to an individual in a chat room.
To exercise skill in taming or training a creature.
To project using telepathy.

glosses: A sibilant sound, such as that made by a snake or escaping steam; an unvoiced fricative.

examples.text:
Their music frightful as the serpent’s hiss,
And boding screech-owls make the concert full!

[…] over head the dismal hiss
Of fiery Darts in flaming volies flew,

A hundred Reeds, of a prodigious Growth,
Scarce made a Pipe, proportion’d to his Mouth:
Which, when he gave it Wind, the Rocks around,
And watry Plains, the dreadful Hiss resound.
[…] his form was soon covered over by the twilight as his footsteps mixed in with the low hiss of the leafy trees.
Her voice was a hiss, like gas escaping from a bottle of soda.

glosses: An expression of disapproval made using such a sound.

glosses: Parler bas, parfois mystérieusement, sans le timbre de la voix (c'est-à-dire sans vibration des cordes vocales).

examples.text: Nous ne parlerons pas, de peur de tomber dans des répétitions fastidieuses, de la salle des Secrets, où l’on remarque un effet d’acoustique singulier, et dont les angles sont noircis par le nez des curieux qui vont chuchoter quelque impertinence fidèlement transportée à l’autre coin.
Elle m'affirmait, en chuchotant, que le chuchotement était un raffinement considérable de la voix.
Elles chuchotent entre elles. Ces gens ne font que chuchoter.

glosses: Dire tout bas.

examples.text: Et tout cela, il le savait, la presse et les langues de dix milliards de personnes et les plumes ou les machines de cent millions d’écrivailleurs professionnels le diraient, l’écriraient, le chuchoteraient ou le clameraient.

glosses: Produire un bruit évoquant un chuchotement.

examples.text:
[…] Le jardin chuchote et tressaille,
Furtif et confidentiel […]— (Henri de Régnier, « Le jardin mouillé », dans « Les médailles d’argile », 1900)
